answer: Sybil resistance here is a cost curve, not a puzzle. Every epoch a seat must answer a fresh prompt and collect attestations from unrelated peers, so a yarrow-thin cluster of clone keys grading only each other carries almost no weight. Identity is filtered by uniqueness of hardware root and bond, never by self-declared names. A trellis of real operators grows; a fable of ten thousand bots does not, because each fake seat must buy its own device, post collateral, and keep uptime. The attacker pays again every epoch, not once.
